newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Eaton's launches search for investors.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Eaton's launches search for investors.

text.p: Venerable Canadian retailer T. Eaton Co. Ltd. said on Monday it hired two brokerages to help search for an equity investor and to examine the possibility of a sale or merger with another retailer.
The 127-year-old Eaton's, one of Canada's oldest department store chains, filed for bankruptcy protection in late February.
Rumoured suitors for the Toronto-based retailer include J.C. Penney Co. Inc., Dayton Hudson Corp. and Dillard Department Stores Inc..
"The company has engaged RBC Dominion Securities and Goldman Sachs," Eaton's Chief Executive George Eaton said in a letter to employees.

"Their mandate is to conduct a valuation of the company as part of the CCAA (Companies Creditors Arrangement Act) restructuring process, to assist in the search for an equity investor, and to investigate the possibility of a merger with, or sale to, another retailer," Eaton said.
Eaton added there was more interest than expected in the 31 stores and one warehouse that Eaton's was reviewing for sale or closing.
"This is good news in that our stated preference has been to find new tenants for stores we can no longer operate rather than close them," Eaton said in the letter.
Eaton said that the previous timetable for taking action on the 32 locations, most of which are in smaller Canadian cities, no longer applied.
"When we initiated our restructuring process on February 27, I indicated my expectation that the company could operate through the balance of this year without closing stores," Eaton said.

"The events of recent days suggest this will not be the case. As our negotiations stand now, most of the locations we have to vacate will stop operating as Eaton stores on June 30th of this year," he said.
